messages.author: 188284624df874cb
messages.subject: Multiple session (Years) and trapping grids
parts:
Hello Group,

I am interested in estimating the change in density of a population (bears) over time using D~ Session where session is the year. I have multiple years of data where trap layout , the number of occasions and usage varies among years (extent doesn't change much). I have different trap files for each session(year) however I am uncertain how to deal with the trap files for the missing sessions(years). If I ignore them everything runs fine but I know this is not legit. I am also concerned how this will affect the later use of spatial masks.

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks in advance,

Michelle


#example of my capture file

 #Year IDS Occasion TRAP_ID Sex HTorRT
2006 F106 1 57HT F HT
2006 F113 1 57HT F HT
2007 F113 1 61HT F HT
2008 NONE 1
2009 NONE 1

################################belwo is the code that I have used we #have no data from 2008, 2009, 2015

traps <- c(
  dSC2006 = "dSC2006.txt",
  dSC2007 = "dSC2007.txt",
  dSC2010 = "dSC2010.txt",
  dSC2011 = "dSC2011.txt",
  dSC2012 = "dSC2012.txt",
  dSC2013 = "dSC2013.txt", 
  dSC2014 = "dSC2014.txt",
  dSC2016 = "dSC2016.txt")


captures = c("SCcapt.txt")


SC_CH <- read.capthist(captures,traps,fmt= "trapID", detector= "proximity", binary.usage=TRUE, covname= c('Sex','HTorRT'),trapcov = c('Year','HTorRT'), noncapt = "NONE")

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multiple session (Years) and trapping grids
parts:
Hi Michelle
I'm not clear on the missing years: presumably there was no sampling effort in those years? If so then there was no relevant trap file and it is not appropriate to include a dummy row ('NONE') in the capture file*. I understand that you are concerned to allow for the spacing of sampling years when fitting the trend model; for that you should provide a session covariate (argument 'sessioncov', one row per session, in order). Something like this should work
secr.fit(SC_CH, ..., sessioncov=data.frame(year = c(2006,2007,2010,2011,2012,2013,2015,2016)), model = D~year)
Multiple year-specific masks can be provided as a list, one component per year. Better documentation is coming!
Murray

* I think your example might fail anyway because there were only 3 columns in those years.

I really appreciate you taking the time to help. You were correct, there was no sampling effort in 2008, 2009 and 2015. I did as you suggested and removed the dummy row (and associated trap files).

 I have attached the trace output from fitting the model. Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
Michelle

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multiple session (Years) and trapping grids
parts:
Hi Michelle
I haven't had that problem, but I can see how it might happen. With the default maximisation method there is a big step away from the starting values at about that iteration, and the slope coefficient went crazy, wildly inappropriate for a model for density on the log scale. I am surprised the algorithm didn't recover, as it usually does, so I'll look into that. The easiest fix is to try method = "Nelder-Mead" in secr.fit. I also guess that the original method might work with typsize = c(1, 0.01, 1, 1) included in the secr.fit call, or with link = list(D="identity"). I'm interested to hear how you go.
Murray

Thank you Murray for your suggestions I tried them all to see how they went: 

1) Including typsize = c(1, 0.01, 1, 1) in the secr.fit call was successful (and quicker). the resulting estimates were credible and reflected the missing sampling years. 

> fit_SC_trend<-secr.fit(SC_CH, mask= mask, sessioncov=data.frame(year = c(2006,2007,2010, 2011,2012,2013,2014,2016)), typsize = c(1, 0.01, 1, 1) , model = D~year)

On Thu, Mar 30, 2017 at 7:10 PM, Murray Efford <murray...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Michelle
I'm not clear on the missing years: presumably there was no sampling effort in those years? If so then there was no relevant trap file and it is not appropriate to include a dummy row ('NONE') in the capture file*. I understand that you are concerned to allow for the spacing of sampling years when fitting the trend model; for that you should provide a session covariate (argument 'sessioncov', one row per session, in order). Something like this should work
secr.fit(SC_CH, ..., sessioncov=data.frame(year = c(2006,2007,2010,2011,2012,2013,2015,2016)), model = D~year)
Multiple year-specific masks can be provided as a list, one component per year. Better documentation is coming!
Murray

* I think your example might fail anyway because there were only 3 columns in those years.
